findings.text: follow-on: the sibling fallback _release_scratch_when_release_raised returns scratch_removed, scratch_path, scratch_withheld and scratch_bytes but omits scratch_removed_paths in its except branch, so a release that raises inside the fallback still yields a receipt whose key set disagrees between the two release surfaces, the same consistency this delta just closed elsewhere.

item_verdicts.diff: read commit by commit. af68a79d2 (test only) has parent 11a9a5573; c3197094b (fix only) adds the single whitelist key plus the docstring wording. No unrelated change, no rename, and no plan, sprint or ticket identifier in code, tests or commit messages.
item_verdicts.done_when: the two commits in scope implement the recorded gap and prove it: af68a79d2 adds tests/test_a_release_removes_all_worker_scratch.py::test_discard_names_each_removed_scratch_directory, which drives crew.discard over a run whose worker left files under both the recorded scratch dir (5 bytes) and a bare-id sibling (6 bytes), and asserts both directories are gone and both named with their sizes in the returned receipt; c3197094b adds "scratch_removed_paths" to the discard projection whitelist and widens the function docstring from worktree-only to worktree-and-scratch. The plan section done-when is met by the reviewed run overall across f87d778c..c3197094b; this delta carries the receipt-consistency half the prior review flagged.
item_verdicts.goal: the reviewed delta closes the one follow-on the prior review recorded for run r-20261004T041323040789: discard and promotion release receipts now agree about removed worker scratch, because _remove_discarded_worktree surfaces scratch_removed_paths from the shared release step (reckon/crew/promotion.py:8366), so a discarded run reports each removed path and its byte count, including a timestamp-stem sibling, exactly as a promoted run does.
item_verdicts.manifest: read; the reviewed run's manifest records the commit list ending c3197094b, the declared negative control (the base release leaves the bare-id sibling), the discard red arm at 11a9a5573 and the three-file after-suite at c3197094b (57 passed, EXIT=0), and a completed status.
item_verdicts.write_paths: the diff 11a9a5573..c3197094b touches exactly reckon/crew/promotion.py (4 insertions, 3 deletions) and tests/test_a_release_removes_all_worker_scratch.py (37 insertions), both named in this node's review scope; nothing else in the range changed.

justifications.durability: the new test exercises the real discard path with real filesystem state under a temporary RECKON_HOME and monkeypatched scratch root, asserts both directories are gone and both named with their byte counts, and reddens at the base revision, so it is a control that fires rather than a demonstration. Docked one point because the release fallback _release_scratch_when_release_raised returns its own receipt without the new key in its except branch, so the surface asymmetry the node set out to close survives in one unexercised path.
justifications.evidence: both arms reproduce independently here. At base revision 11a9a5573 with the new test overlaid, crew.discard removes both directories (captured stdout names the 5-byte and 6-byte removals) and then fails its receipt assertion with KeyError: 'scratch_removed_paths', EXIT=1; at head c3197094b the same test is 1 passed, EXIT=0, and the reviewed run's own committed after-suite at c3197094b is 57 passed with EXIT=0.
justifications.fit: the change keeps the module's existing whitelist-projection idiom and dict-result shape, adds no rename, updates the docstring to describe the widened field set, and names nothing by plan, sprint, ticket or author.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the delta closes precisely the follow-on the prior review stored against this run, namely that the discard receipt's projected key set omitted scratch_removed_paths, and does so through the shared release step rather than a second policy, so discard and promotion cannot disagree about what was removed.
justifications.scope_discipline: the two commits touch only the two files named as this review's scope; the test-only and fix-only commits are cleanly separated, and there is no in-flight or unrelated edit in the range.
